A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAPPA study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original probing, intervention, cross-dataset transfer and free-form generation results, including Tables 1–4 and appendix Tables 11–12.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations and adds geometric measurements, larger-model experiments, sensitivity tests and transfer-loss analyses.

M1.justification: The two probes, minimal-perturbation intervention, alpha/beta alignment and token-wise application are retained. The corrected main update matches the solution already derived in v3 Appendix B.1. Centered subspaces are introduced for geometric analysis, without establishing a changed KAPPA intervention procedure.

E1.justification: The benchmark datasets, subtasks and free-form evaluation tasks are retained. Distractor resampling and training subsets remain within existing coverage; Qwen3-32B extends model configurations. The GSM8k-MCQ source is newly identified, without evidence that the underlying dataset changed.

E2.justification: Base, CAA, DoLA and KP remain in the corresponding performance comparisons, and CAA/DoLA procedures are unchanged. New random-subspace controls support geometric diagnostics rather than introducing an evaluated competing intervention.

E3.justification: v4 adds principal-angle and CKA evaluation with random controls, cross-benchmark correlation protocols, Qwen3-32B and alpha=80 configurations, distractor-resampled testing, and retraining on 10–80% subsets. These substantially extend experimental design; the original splits, probe-training settings and main evaluation pipeline remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's logit visualization, hyperparameter sweep and transfer analyses, v4 adds quantitative subspace geometry, comparison with the unembedding space, distractor and training-size sensitivity, and correct-to-incorrect transfer analysis. Sections 4 and 6 and Appendices B/E substantially expand tests of mechanism, robustness and failure conditions.

E5.justification: v4 adds accuracy means and standard deviations across 10 distractor seeds, one-sided t-tests, three-seed training-subset averages, Spearman correlations with p-values, and random-control sampling details. These reporting practices were absent from v3 and concern the new analyses, not documented repetitions of all retained results.

E6.justification: v4 adds geometric, sensitivity, larger-model and transfer-loss results. Tables 2–3 revise Llama TruthfulQA KAPPA(3)/(6) accuracy from 73.5/65.5 to 65.6/73.5; Table 2 also revises Llama BBH-Algorithmic KAPPA(3) ACC/AGR from 49.2/81.9 to 49.5/82.9. New Table 13 reports Qwen3-32B accuracy of 84.0 with alpha=80 versus 79.5 for Base.

T1.justification: v4 formally defines decision-relevant subspaces using mean-centered weights with rank at most k−1. It also corrects the main closed-form expression to use the unaugmented prediction-weight Gram matrix, resolving its inconsistency with v3's existing appendix derivation. The underlying optimization and Lagrange-multiplier proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: a widespread MCQ knowledge-prediction gap, a geometric account involving knowledge/prediction subspaces, and mitigation through KAPPA with some transfer beyond MCQs. The additional analyses principally strengthen support for these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v4 develops an abstract-feature explanation of KAPPA using separation from the unembedding space, explains how near-orthogonal subspaces can retain correlated representations, and discusses scale and distillation as possible causes. Appendix E.4 adds task-specific transfer-failure interpretations. Section 3 also softens v3's inference that underusing linear knowledge makes effective nonlinear knowledge use implausible.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the future code-release promise with a repository link and identifies the GSM8k-MCQ source. New appendices document centering, SVD rank tolerance, random-subspace construction, unembedding extraction and sampling/retraining recipes, substantially extending reproducibility information without establishing changes to the original training setup.

R1.justification: Related Work replaces some safety/toxicity/reasoning-steering examples with sentiment, personality and value-direction studies, including Tigges, Han and Jha. New references support CKA, logit-lens and feature-geometry discussions and identify the GSM8k-MCQ source. The central positioning connecting gap diagnosis with inference-time intervention remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and analysis narrative are substantially rewritten. Geometric analysis becomes a standalone section, and the appendices reorganize previously separate data, prompting, evaluation and probing material into a consolidated setup appendix, followed by geometry, derivation, baselines and results. Explanations and cross-references are extensively revised.

P2.justification: v4 adds dedicated geometry, correlation, training-size and gain/loss displays in Figures 8–14, plus Tables 13–15. Existing displays are relocated; Table 1 changes highlighting, and Figure 3 gains Pearson-correlation annotations and a revised caption. The original plotted data in Figures 1–7 are retained.

improvement.justification: v3's geometric explanation relied mainly on logit scatter plots. v4 substantially strengthens that central argument with centered-subspace measurements, random controls and cross-benchmark tests, while seeded sensitivity experiments and transfer-loss reporting improve assessment of robustness and limitations. The main update also becomes consistent with the existing derivation. Qwen's correlation remains nonsignificant and some mechanistic/distillation explanations remain inferential, but the added validation provides a substantial net quality improvement.
